【P1｜Mr. Utterson】
别称：G. J. Utterson、Gabriel John Utterson、Utterson
当前一句话身份：Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
档案（最新）：occupation：lawyer；personality：uneasy and concerned for Jekyll；situation：last good influence on downgoing men；residence：bachelor house near a church；identity：lawyer
关系：Mr. Richard Enfield（cousin）、Dr. Jekyll（client and friend whose affairs he handles）、Dr. Lanyon（friend who left him a narrative）、Sir Danvers Carew（lawyer who identifies him）、Inspector Newcomen of Scotland Yard（police officer assisting him）、Mr. Guest（employee）、Bradshaw（subordinate）、Poole（butler of Jekyll who assists him）、the man in the middle（beneficiary named in Jekyll's earlier will）
至今经历（按时间）：
- Utterson greets Jekyll and hopes he is better.
- Utterson introduces his cousin Mr. Enfield to Dr. Jekyll and invites Jekyll out.
- Utterson proposes they stay below and talk from where they are.
- The two men leave the court in silence, pale with horror.
- Utterson says 'God forgive us' twice.
- Poole comes to Utterson's house at night and says something is wrong.
- Poole says the doctor has shut himself in the cabinet and he is afraid.
- Poole says he thinks there has been foul play.
- Utterson rises, takes hat and greatcoat, and follows Poole.
- They walk through the cold deserted London streets to the house.
- They enter the hall where all the servants are huddled in fear.
- The housemaid whimpers and the maid weeps loudly.
- Poole leads Utterson to the laboratory and tells him to listen quietly.
- Poole asks whether that was his master's voice; Utterson says it seems much changed.
- Utterson calls the tale wild and argues a murderer would not stay.
- Poole hands Utterson a crumpled note from Dr. Jekyll to Messrs. Maw.
- Utterson notes the handwriting is the doctor's; Poole says he has seen him.
- Poole tells Utterson he saw a masked figure in the cabinet.
- Utterson suggests Jekyll suffers a deforming disease and hides his face.
- Poole insists the masked thing was not Jekyll but a dwarf.
- Utterson resolves to break in the cabinet door.
- Poole and Utterson agree to break in together.
- Poole fetches an axe and suggests Utterson take the kitchen poker.
- Utterson warns Poole they are placing themselves in peril.
- Poole says the masked figure was Mr. Hyde.
- Utterson says he once spoke with Hyde.
- Poole describes Hyde as giving a cold, thin feeling.
- Utterson summons Bradshaw and orders him to guard the laboratory door.
- Poole and Utterson wait in the theatre and hear pacing footsteps.
- Poole says the walker weeps like a woman or lost soul.
- Utterson demands to see Jekyll and threatens brute force.
- The voice begs Utterson for mercy.
- Utterson recognizes the voice as Hyde's and orders the door down.
- They peer in and find the contorted body of Edward Hyde.
- Utterson concludes Hyde is a self-destroyer by the crushed phial.
- Utterson says they must now find Jekyll's body.
- Utterson and Poole search the theatre, cabinet, closets and cellar for Jekyll.
- They find the by-street door locked with a rusty broken key lying nearby.
- They examine the cabinet and find chemical apparatus and white salt on saucers.
- They find a pious book annotated by Jekyll with startling blasphemies.
- They look into the cheval-glass and see only the room and their own pale faces.
- Utterson opens an envelope addressed to him and finds a will naming himself instead of Hyde.
- Utterson reads Jekyll's dated note and concludes Jekyll was alive that day and may have fled.
- Poole hands Utterson a sealed packet, the third enclosure.
- Utterson decides to go home, read the documents, and return before midnight to send for the police.
